nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a program with $g$ gates over $m$ inputs, let $c \in \mathbb{N}$, and for each $j < c$ let $f_j$ be a line that reads the inputs and the first $g + j$ gates. Under any interpretation of the gate symbols and any input values, for every $k < g$ the value of gate $k$ of the program obtained by appending $f_0, \dots, f_{c-1}$ to $p$ equals the value of gate $k$ of $p$.

nodes.summary: For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the carry depth of bit $i$ is $0$ if $i = 0$ and $2i + 1$ if $i \ge 1$. It is used as the depth of the carry into bit $i$ of the ripple-carry adder, where the carry into bit $0$ is the carry-in input.
nodes.title: Carry depth in the ripple-carry adder

Evaluate the $n$-bit Kogge-Stone carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels over the Boolean XOR/AND/OR basis on the input that lists the bits of $x$ from least to most significant, then those of $y$ in the same order, then $c$. nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 2$, the $n$-bit Kogge-Stone carry-lookahead adder with $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ levels has depth exactly $2 \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 5$, the depth being the largest depth of an output with the inputs at depth $0$.
nodes.title: Depth of the carry-lookahead adder with logarithmically many levels

nodes.title: Exact depth of the carry-lookahead adder

nodes.summary: For all $n, K \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-bit Kogge-Stone carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels has exactly $5n + 3nK$ gates: $2n$ in the first level, $3n$ in each of the $K$ Kogge-Stone levels, and $3n$ in the final level.
nodes.title: Gate count of the carry-lookahead adder

nodes.summary: Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a carry-in bit and $K$ a natural number with $n \le 2^K$. Evaluate the $n$-bit Kogge–Stone carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels in the Boolean interpretation of the XOR/AND/OR basis, on the input made of the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ of the adder is bit $i$ (the bit of weight $2^i$) of the sum $x + y + c$ taken modulo $2^n$.
nodes.title: Sum bits of the carry-lookahead adder

For $i < n$, output $i$ is the sum gate of bit $i$ in the…

nodes.title: Depth of the sum gates

nodes.title: Gates of the carry-lookahead adder

nodes.summary: For pairs of Booleans $(G, P)$ and $(G', P')$, their combination is $(G \lor (P \land G'), P \land P')$.
nodes.title: Combining generate–propagate pairs

nodes.summary: For each gate of the arithmetic basis (XOR, AND or OR) and all argument depths $d_0, d_1 \in \mathbb{N}$, the depth interpretation of the arithmetic signature assigns the gate the depth $\max(d_0, d_1) + 1$.
nodes.title: Depth of an arithmetic gate

nodes.summary: For a signature $\sigma$, the depth interpretation is the interpretation of $\sigma$ in $\mathbb{N}$ that sends an operation symbol of arity $k$, applied to argument depths $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$, to $\max(0, d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}) + 1$: a gate is one deeper than its deepest argument, and a gate without arguments has depth $1$.
nodes.title: The depth interpretation

nodes.summary: For every program $p$ over a signature $\sigma$, the depth of each gate of $p$ equals the value of that gate when $p$ is evaluated under the depth interpretation of $\sigma$ with every input set to $0$.
nodes.title: Gate depths are evaluation in the depth interpretation

nodes.summary: For $n$-bit Kogge-Stone adders, the generate signal of bit $i$ after level $0$ is held by gate $2i$, and after Kogge-Stone level $k + 1$ by gate $2n + 3nk + 3i + 1$; here $2n + 3nk$ is the number of gates in levels $0, \dots, k$.
nodes.title: Index of the generate gate

nodes.summary: Let $c(i)$ be the carry depth of bit $i$: $c(0) = 0$ and $c(i) = 2i + 1$ for $i \ge 1$. The formula assigns to gate $j$ of the ripple-carry adder, for every $j \in \mathbb{N}$, the depth $1$ when $j \bmod 5$ is $0$ or $2$, the depth $\max(1, c(\lfloor j/5 \rfloor)) + 1$ when $j \bmod 5$ is $1$ or $3$, and the depth $c(\lfloor j/5 \rfloor + 1)$ when $j \bmod 5 = 4$.
nodes.title: Gate-depth formula for the ripple-carry adder

nodes.summary: For bit vectors $x, y$ of width $n$ and an index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the generate–propagate pair of bit $i$ is $(x_i \wedge y_i,\ x_i \oplus y_i)$, where $x_i$ and $y_i$ are bit $i$ of $x$ and $y$, taken to be false when $i \ge n$.
nodes.title: Generate and propagate signals of a bit

nodes.summary: Fix bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width, write $\mathrm{GP}(\ell, m)$ for the generate–propagate pair of the block of the $m$ bits $\ell, \dots, \ell + m - 1$, and write $h \circ l$ for the block operator with $h$ placed above $l$. Then for all natural numbers $\ell, a, b$, $\mathrm{GP}(\ell, a + b) = \mathrm{GP}(\ell + a, b) \circ \mathrm{GP}(\ell, a)$.
nodes.title: Adjacent blocks compose

nodes.summary: For bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width, a start bit $\ell$ and a length $m$, the generate–propagate pair $\mathrm{GP}(\ell, m)$ of the block of bits $\ell, \dots, \ell + m - 1$ is defined by recursion on $m$: the empty block has $\mathrm{GP}(\ell, 0) = (\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true})$, and $\mathrm{GP}(\ell, m + 1) = \mathrm{gp}(\ell + m) \circ \mathrm{GP}(\ell, m)$, where $\mathrm{gp}(\ell + m)$ is the…
nodes.title: Generate and propagate signals of a block

nodes.summary: Fix bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width and write $S_k(i)$ for the generate–propagate pair of the block of the $\min(i + 1, 2^k)$ bits ending at bit $i$, the pair bit $i$ holds after $k$ Kogge-Stone levels. For all $k, i \in \mathbb{N}$: if $2^k \le i$, then $S_{k+1}(i) = S_k(i) \circ S_k(i - 2^k)$, where $\circ$ is the block operator with its left argument placed above its right; otherwise $S_{k+1}(i) = S_k(i)$.
nodes.title: The Kogge-Stone step

nodes.summary: Fix bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width. For $k, i \in \mathbb{N}$, the pair $S_k(i)$ that bit $i$ holds after $k$ Kogge-Stone levels is the generate–propagate pair of the block of the $\min(i + 1, 2^k)$ bits ending at bit $i$, that is, of the bits $i + 1 - \min(i + 1, 2^k), \dots, i$.
nodes.title: The block held after Kogge-Stone levels

nodes.summary: For an $n$-bit adder, the number $L_n(k)$ of gates in level $0$ together with the first $k$ Kogge-Stone levels is given by $L_n(0) = 2n$ and $L_n(k + 1) = L_n(k) + 3n$, so $L_n(k) = 2n + 3nk$.
nodes.title: Gate count of the first Kogge-Stone levels

nodes.summary: In the program made of level $0$ and the first $k$ Kogge-Stone levels of the $n$-bit adder, where inputs have depth $0$ and a gate is one deeper than its deepest argument, for every bit $i < n$ the gate holding the generate signal of bit $i$ has depth $2k + 1$ and the gate holding its propagate signal has depth $k + 1$.
nodes.title: Depths after each level

nodes.summary: For the $n$-bit adder, every interpretation of the XOR, AND and OR gates in a type $U$, every assignment of values in $U$ to the $2n + 1$ inputs, and every $K$, each of the $2n$ gates of level $0$ has the same value in the program with level $0$ and $K$ Kogge-Stone levels as in the program with level $0$ alone.
nodes.title: Level-0 gates are unchanged by later levels

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a carry bit, and evaluate level $0$ and the first $k$ Kogge-Stone levels of the adder on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. For every bit $i < n$, the gate holding the generate signal of bit $i$ carries the generate signal, and the gate holding its propagate signal carries the propagate signal, of the block of the at most $2^k$ bits ending at $i$, that is, of the…
nodes.title: Each Kogge-Stone level is correct

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a carry bit, and evaluate level $0$ of the adder on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. For every bit $i < n$, the gate holding the generate signal of bit $i$ carries the generate signal, and the gate holding its propagate signal carries the propagate signal, of the block consisting of bit $i$ alone, namely $x_i \wedge y_i$ and $x_i \oplus y_i$.
nodes.title: Level 0 computes generate and propagate

nodes.summary: For an $n$-bit adder, the program over the XOR, AND and OR gates on $2n + 1$ inputs obtained from the empty program by appending the $2n$ gates of level $0$ and then, in turn, the $3n$ gates of each Kogge-Stone level $1, \dots, k$. It has $2n + 3nk$ gates.

Write $G_i$ and $P_i$ for the generate and propagate gates of bit $i$ after the $K$ levels, $p_i$ for the propagate gate of bit $i$ at level $0$, and $c$ for the carry input. If $j \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ the gate computes $P_i \wedge c$; if $j \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ it computes the carry…
nodes.title: Gates of the final level

nodes.summary: Gate $j < 3n$ of Kogge-Stone level $k + 1$ of the $n$-bit adder serves bit $i = \lfloor j/3 \rfloor$ and its partner $q$, which is $i - 2^k$ if $2^k \le i$ and $i$ otherwise. Write $G_b$ and $P_b$ for the generate and propagate gates of bit $b$ after level $k$. nodes.title: Gates of a Kogge-Stone level

nodes.summary: Gate $j < 2n$ of level $0$ of the $n$-bit adder of $x$ and $y$ reads the inputs $\lfloor j/2 \rfloor$ and $n + \lfloor j/2 \rfloor$, which carry bit $\lfloor j/2 \rfloor$ of $x$ and of $y$. For even $j$ it is an AND gate, the generate signal of that bit; for odd $j$ it is an XOR gate, its propagate signal.
nodes.title: Gates of level 0

nodes.summary: The lowest bit of the block that bit $i$ holds after $k$ Kogge-Stone levels, $i + 1 - \min(i + 1, 2^k)$, that is, $\max(0, i + 1 - 2^k)$.
nodes.title: Lowest bit of a Kogge-Stone block

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $i$, $p_n(k, i)$ is the index of the gate holding the propagate signal of bit $i$ after level $k$ of the $n$-bit carry-lookahead adder: $p_n(0, i) = 2i + 1$, and $p_n(k + 1, i) = 2n + 3nk + 3i + 2$, where $2n + 3nk$ is the number of gates in levels $0, \dots, k$.
nodes.title: Propagate gate of a bit in the Kogge–Stone adder

nodes.summary: The bit combined with bit $i$ at level $k + 1$ of the Kogge–Stone adder is bit $i - 2^k$ if $2^k \le i$, and bit $i$ itself otherwise.
nodes.title: Kogge–Stone partner bit

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $g \le 5n$ and $j < g$, evaluating the first $g$ gates of the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder in $\mathbb{N}$, with every input at depth $0$ and every gate one deeper than its deepest argument, gives gate $j$ the depth $d(j)$. Here, with $q = \lfloor j / 5 \rfloor$, $c(0) = 0$ and $c(i) = 2i + 1$ for $i \ge 1$, $d(j) = 1$ if $j \bmod 5 \in \{0, 2\}$, $d(j) = \max(1, c(q)) + 1$ if…
nodes.title: Gate depths of the ripple-carry adder

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder has depth $2n + 1$, the length of its carry chain.
nodes.title: The ripple-carry adder has linear depth

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
